In [[geometry]], the '''elongated cupolae''' are an infinite set of polyhedra, constructed by adjoining an ''n''-gonal [[Cupola (geometry)|cupola]] to a 2''n''-gonal [[Prism (geometry)|prism]].

There are three ''elongated cupolae'' that are [[Johnson solid]]s made from regular triangles, squares, and pentagons. Higher forms can be constructed with isosceles triangles. Adjoining a [[triangular prism]] to a cube also generates a polyhedron, but has two pairs of coplanar faces, so is not a Johnson solid. Higher forms can be constructed without regular faces.
